draft.title: Projectile motion
card: A projectile is an object moving through the air under gravity alone. Here we ignore air resistance.
no force acts sideways, so the horizontal velocity stays constant and the acceleration is zero.
gravity pulls down, so the vertical velocity changes by 9.8 m/s every second. The acceleration is 9.8 m/s² downwards, whether the object is rising or falling.
The two directions do not affect each other, so we solve them separately. Time is the link: it is the same for both.
draft.remember: Treat horizontal and vertical separately: constant velocity sideways, constant acceleration downwards.

a.q: A ball rolls off a table and flies through the air. Ignoring air resistance, which statement describes its motion?
opts: Sideways velocity is constant, falling velocity changes
Both horizontal and vertical velocities are constant
Horizontal velocity decreases as the ball falls
Vertical velocity is constant at 9.8 m/s
a.why: No horizontal force acts, so horizontal velocity stays the same. Gravity changes the vertical velocity. The option saying 9.8 m/s is tempting, but 9.8 is the acceleration in m/s², not a constant speed.
a.clue: Which direction has a force acting on it?

b.q: Priya kicks a ball horizontally off a cliff at 12 m/s. At the same instant, Sam drops a second ball from rest off the same cliff. Ignoring air resistance, how do their times to reach the ground compare?
opts: They land at the same time
Priya's ball lands later because it travels further
b.why: Both balls start with zero vertical velocity and have the same vertical acceleration and height, so the vertical motion is identical. Priya's ball moves sideways too, but that does not change the time it takes to fall.
b.clue: Does sideways motion change how fast something falls?

a.best: Sideways velocity is constant, falling velocity changes

b.best: They land at the same time
